filter.inkscape:menu-tooltip: Like Duochrome but with three colors

tspan.tspan: COCKPIT CROSS POINTER
The CROSS POINTER is a primary instrument for commanding input to
the spacecraft autopilot in conjunction with the radar system or
IMU. The background card has five concentric circles representing
steps of 1 or 10 (for X5 and X50 ranges, respectively). The LOS
(Loss Of Signal) indicator is a red light that illuminates when the
cross pointer is not receiving updates from the radar or IMU.
The ORANGE vertical and horizontal indicator bars display deviation
from center of a measured parameter. With HVEL RADAR active, they
show left-right and forward-reverse HVEL speeds respectively, 1 m/s
per division in X5 mode or 10 m/s per division in X50 mode.
The GREEN diamonds show the pilot command when the autopilot is
engaged. The autopilot seeks to align the bars with the diamonds.
CROSS POINTER CONTROLS
XPTR AUTO: When illuminated, the X50 range will activate automatically when either indicator
bar goes off-scale, and the X5 range will activate when both indicator bars are at or below 5
units (m/s in RADAR mode). When not extinguished, the X5 and X50 ranges are under pilot manual
control.
X5: When illuminated, the indicator bars measure 5 units (m/s in RADAR mode) at the outermost
circle.
X50: When illuminated, the indicator bars measure 50 units (m/s in RADAR mode) at the outermost
circle.
